title: Indicators, decisions and doubt
summary: What an indicator describes, why to write your reason first, and how to test an idea fairly.

steps.head: What an indicator is
steps.body: An {{indicator|indicator}} is a number worked out from past prices. It sums up what has already happened.

steps.head: The 20-day average
steps.body: The 20-day average is the mean of the last 20 closing prices. A price above it has been higher lately than its usual level. It says nothing about tomorrow.
steps.more: A moving average follows the price with a delay, because it is built from old prices.

steps.head: The RSI
steps.body: The {{rsi|RSI}} compares recent rises with recent falls, on a scale from 0 to 100. A high RSI says the last days were mostly rises. It does not say a fall is due.

steps.head: Write your reason first
steps.body: A {{decision-journal|decision journal}} keeps what you chose and why, before you know the result. Later you cannot rewrite what you thought.
steps.more: After a result, the past often looks obvious. Your own written reason is the fair record.

steps.head: Testing an idea fairly
steps.body: A rule built on an indicator is one more {{idea-tried|idea tried}}. Test it with costs, on new prices, and count your tries.

options.text: The mean of the last 20 closing prices.
options.why: Yes. It sums up the recent past, nothing more.
No. An average is built from old prices, so it cannot see ahead.

options.text: A sure sign of what to hold.
options.why: No. It describes the past. It is not a promise about the future.

questions.prompt: An RSI of 80 says the last days were mostly rises. Does it say a fall is due?

options.text: No. It describes the past only.
options.why: Right. A high RSI tells you how the last days went, not what comes next.

options.text: Yes. A high RSI always means a fall.
options.why: No. Prices can keep rising after a high RSI, and they can fall after a low one.
No. Nothing about the RSI fixes a date or a direction.

questions.prompt: Why write your reason before you see the result?

options.text: So hindsight cannot rewrite what you thought.
options.why: Right. Your own words from that day are the fair record to learn from.
No. Writing first does not change the result. It keeps your record honest.

options.text: Because the result is always wrong.
options.why: No. Results are sometimes right and sometimes wrong. A reason helps you tell luck from judgement.
